prompt:
Precise PROPORTION HARMONIZATION of the butterfly mage in IMAGE 1 to join the same game cast as IMAGES 2 and 3.
Image1 is the ONLY character to redraw. Images2/3 supply the actual head-to-body proportion standard and NOTHING else. Do NOT copy their adult faces/physiques, costumes or weapons. Keep the youthful butterfly girl's gentle round face and wholesome fully covered outfit.

The current image1 actual head is too small and body/legs too long. Make a decisive visible anatomical redraw to approximately FOUR REAL HEAD HEIGHTS from anatomical CROWN to BOOT SOLES. Head unit = actual skull/hair crown to CHIN; do NOT count the tall butterfly antennas, floating talismans, ponytail or cloak extensions as head or body height.
Increase the actual head/skull/face size by approximately 25–30 percent relative to the body. Modestly shorten torso and neck; shorten thigh and shin lengths evenly about 15–20 percent, preserving naturally light slender youthful limbs. Keep the hands and boots anatomically proportionate. Do not make her heavy or barrel-shaped; do not apply a simple vertical/horizontal squeeze. Match the head/body relationship of images2/3 while retaining image1's younger face. The actual head must read as about one quarter of crown-to-sole height.
Keep the long swept butterfly antennas at their existing relative visual length, NOT enlarged along with the head. Reattach them naturally to the enlarged head. Preserve face identity and kind expression. The large cloak still contrasts with her small slender central body and forms a broad triangular silhouette.

Everything else is DESIGN LOCKED:
- same silver-white hair in large painted locks, pointed ears, two swept-back purple antenna ornaments;
- same oversized asymmetric triangular purple butterfly cloak, two large pale cyan/lavender wing motifs and TWO long continuous eye-tipped swallowtail extensions;
- same raised palm and exactly THREE hovering ivory paper talismans with redesigned violet seal strokes and tiny red seals;
- same small yin-yang clasp and restrained cloud motif;
- same modest ivory-violet cross-collar outfit, shorter layered ruqun, continuous fully opaque dark-violet leggings and simple boots. No bare thighs, sheer fabric, adult body sculpting or sexualized pose.
- same coherent front three-quarter LEFT orientation, gentle asymmetrical weight shift, both hands correctly connected, two separate legs and boots with clear anatomy. Adjust arms/legs organically to the new lengths without losing the pose.
- same strong dark contours, simplified matte hand-painted gem-icon color planes. Avoid adding extra tiny shards; consolidate overly fragmented hair shadows if needed into broad groups.

Redraw cloth attachment/folds to fit the corrected compact figure. Keep full antennas, three talismans, two long tails and both boots in the square canvas with safe margins. Warm uniform ivory background, no inset rectangle, labels, comparison sheet or extra people. Output one improved character only.
FINAL CHECK: actual crown-to-chin head vs actual crown-to-sole body should be roughly 1:4, independent of tall decorations. The change from image1 should be clearly visible as a larger real head and more compact torso/legs, not merely different framing.
purpose: Harmonize actual crown-to-chin head versus crown-to-sole body proportions with the project female blade and archer, excluding ornaments.
visual_review: Real head is visibly larger relative to shorter torso/legs; silhouette and costume retained. Approximate four-head proportion is a visual design target, not an exact measured claim.
